entries.title: My shape is not closed
entries.q: open contour; not closed; gap; wont extrude; cannot extrude; extrude error; sketch has open; broken outline; ends not touching; wont let me extrude; cant extrude; extrude not working; extrude error; shape wont fill; outline not solid; wont turn 3d; sketch not closed; missing line; hole in outline
entries.fix: Find the gap in your outline and drag one loose end onto the other until it snaps.

steps.t: Zoom in on every corner with the scroll wheel. A gap can be too small to see from far away.
Open the Tools menu, then Sketch Tools, then Check Sketch for Feature. Click Check. It tells you where the open ends are.
Click and drag one loose end onto the other end. Let go when a small orange square appears. That square means the two ends are joined.
Delete any tiny extra line you find. Click it, press Delete.
Try the extrude again.

entries.why: An extrude pushes your outline into 3D, like pouring plastic into a mold. If the outline has a gap, the plastic leaks out, so SolidWorks refuses. Every outline must be one closed loop.

entries.title: It says my sketch has multiple contours or lines crossing
entries.q: multiple contours; self intersecting; lines crossing; overlapping lines; two outlines; contour error; intersect
entries.fix: Erase the extra pieces so there is one outline. Circles inside it are fine: they become holes.

steps.t: Look for lines that cross each other or stick out past a corner.
On the Sketch tab, click Trim Entities. Choose Power trim.
Hold the left mouse button and drag across the extra pieces. They disappear as you cross them.
Look for a line drawn twice on top of itself: drag a line away and see if another one is under it. Delete the copy.
Run Tools, Sketch Tools, Check Sketch for Feature to confirm.

entries.why: A hook is one outline with holes inside it. Two outlines side by side, or lines that cross, give SolidWorks more than one possible shape and it cannot guess which one you mean.

entries.title: I left my sketch and cannot get back in
entries.q: exited sketch; get back into sketch; edit sketch; left sketch; cant edit sketch; sketch gone; change my sketch; go back to sketch; go back to my sketch; get back to my sketch; back into my sketch; edit my sketch; edit sketch; open my sketch again; pencil; little pencil; pencil icon; clicked out; pressed escape and lost sketch; how edit drawing; go back to drawing; unlock sketch; get back in my sketch; back in my sketch; get in my sketch
entries.fix: Click the sketch in the tree on the left, then click Edit Sketch (the pencil).

steps.t: Find the list on the left side of the screen. That is the tree: every step of your part, in order.
If you already extruded, click the small arrow next to Boss-Extrude1. Your sketch (Sketch1) is inside it.
Click Sketch1. A small bar of icons pops up next to your mouse.
Click Edit Sketch, the icon with a pencil. Your sketch lines light up and you can change them.
When you finish, click the Exit Sketch icon in the top-right corner of the part area.

entries.why: Leaving a sketch does not lock it. Every sketch and feature stays editable forever. Editing is how you change a part, which is why you never need to start over.

entries.title: I messed up so badly I want to delete everything and start over
entries.q: start over; delete everything; delete part; messed up; ruined; new part again; restart
entries.fix: Do not delete it. Press Ctrl+Z to undo, or edit the step that went wrong. It is almost always faster.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z. Each press undoes one step. Keep going until it looks right again.
If one feature is wrong, right-click it in the tree and pick Edit Feature.
If the shape is wrong, click the sketch in the tree and pick Edit Sketch.
Still stuck after that? Ask a TA before you delete anything.

entries.why: Starting over throws away every correct step with the one wrong one. In CAD you fix the step that broke. The tree is there so you can go back to any step.

entries.title: My numbers are huge or weird, like 25.4
entries.q: millimeters; mm; wrong units; numbers huge; 25.4; metric; inches; units; decimals; numbers look wrong; 25.4; 12.7; millimeter; wrong measurements
entries.fix: You are in millimeters. Click the units at the bottom-right corner and pick IPS.

steps.t: Look at the bottom-right corner of the SolidWorks window. It shows the unit system, like MMGS.
Click it and pick IPS (inch, pound, second).
Your part does not change size. Only the numbers change to inches.
If you typed numbers while in millimeters, they are wrong now. Retype them in inches.
To make three decimal places show: Options (the gear at the top), Document Properties tab, Units, set Length decimals to .123.

entries.why: Every size in this project is in inches. A 2 you typed in millimeters is 2 mm, about the thickness of a coin. The unit system decides what your typed numbers mean.

entries.title: My sketch turned red or yellow, or says Over Defined
entries.q: red lines; yellow lines; over defined; overdefined; conflict; sketch red; cannot solve; sketchxpert; everything red; red lines; turned red; sketch error
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z to undo the last dimension or relation you added.

steps.t: Look at the bottom of the screen. It says Over Defined when two rules are fighting.
Press Ctrl+Z once. That usually removes the rule that caused it.
Or find the red or yellow dimension and delete it.
For help finding it: click the words Over Defined at the bottom. SketchXpert opens. Click Diagnose, pick a solution, click Accept.

entries.why: Each dimension is a rule. If a line is 2 inches long AND its two ends are dimensioned 2.5 inches apart, both cannot be true. SolidWorks shows the conflict in red.

entries.title: What do blue and black lines mean?
entries.q: blue lines; black lines; under defined; fully defined; line colors; why blue
entries.fix: Blue means the line can still move. Black means dimensions lock it in place. Both are fine.

steps.t: Drag a blue line. It moves, because nothing locks it yet.
Add dimensions until the lines turn black. Black lines stay put when you change other things.
The bottom of the screen says Under Defined or Fully Defined.

entries.why: A fully defined sketch (all black) behaves predictably when you change a number. It is good practice, not a requirement for your first part.

entries.title: My part disappeared or I cannot find it
entries.q: cant see part; disappeared; lost; gone; zoomed out; blank screen; where is my part; nothing there; screen empty; white screen; zoomed in too far; cant find anything; where did it go
entries.fix: Put your mouse over the part area and press F. It zooms to fit your whole part.

steps.t: Move the mouse over the big part area and press F.
Still nothing? Press the spacebar and double-click Isometric.
Look in the tree for a gray line with a yellow-and-black bar above your features. Right-click the bar and pick Roll to End.
Open the Solid Bodies folder in the tree. If your body is hidden, right-click it and pick Show.

entries.why: The part is almost never gone. The view moved, the rollback bar hid it, or the body was hidden. None of those delete anything.

entries.title: There is a red X or a yellow triangle in the tree
entries.q: red x; error; yellow triangle; warning; rebuild error; feature failed; fillet failed; cut failed; failed; what wrong; exclamation
entries.fix: Hover over the first one from the top to read what it says, then right-click it and pick Edit Feature.

steps.t: Find the FIRST feature with a mark, counting from the top of the tree. Fix that one first: it often causes the others.
Hover the mouse over it and read the message.
Right-click it. Pick Edit Feature to change its settings, or Edit Sketch to change its shape.
A yellow triangle is a warning: the part still works. A red X means that feature failed.
Common cause: a Fillet radius that is too big. Make it smaller.

entries.why: Features are built in order, top to bottom. If an early one changes, a later one can lose the edge or face it was attached to, and it fails.

entries.title: Things in my tree are gray, or there is a yellow and black line in the middle
entries.q: grayed out; gray features; rollback bar; yellow black line; features missing; part went back
entries.fix: Right-click the yellow and black bar and pick Roll to End.

steps.t: Find the yellow and black bar in the tree.
Right-click it and pick Roll to End. Or drag it to the very bottom.

entries.why: That bar is a time machine. Everything below it is switched off, so you can see the part as it was earlier. Somebody dragged it by accident.

entries.title: It keeps drawing lines every time I click
entries.q: keeps drawing; cant stop drawing; line tool; extra lines; stop tool; stop drawing; how to stop drawing; stop the line
entries.fix: Press Esc. That stops the tool.

steps.t: Press Esc once or twice.
Delete any extra lines: click one, press Delete.

entries.why: The Line tool stays on so you can draw a chain of lines. Esc or a double-click ends the chain.

entries.title: A tool opened that I did not choose
entries.q: tool opened by itself; random tool; enter key; repeat command; popped up; pressed enter; hit enter; something opened; enter opened a tool; enter key
entries.fix: Press Esc to close it. Pressing Enter repeats the last tool you used.

steps.t: Press Esc.
If a panel opened on the left, click the red X at its top.

entries.why: In SolidWorks the Enter key means do the last command again. That is handy once you know it and confusing until you do.

entries.title: I cannot click the face or edge I want
entries.q: cant select; wrong face; clicks wrong thing; select edge; select face; behind; hidden face
entries.fix: Right-click near it, choose Select Other, and pick the one you want from the list.

steps.t: Rotate the view so the face or edge is facing you: hold the middle mouse button and drag.
Or right-click near it and choose Select Other. Move through the list until the right one lights up, and click it.
Zoom in with the scroll wheel so edges are farther apart.

entries.why: SolidWorks picks whatever is closest to the mouse. Thin parts put faces and edges very close together.

entries.title: The buttons or tabs at the top disappeared
entries.q: toolbar gone; tabs missing; commandmanager; buttons gone; sketch tab missing; features tab missing; ribbon gone; tool bar gone; toolbar gone; tabs gone; tabs disappeared; ribbon gone; buttons gone
entries.fix: Right-click on any tab at the top (like Features) and turn on the tab you are missing.

steps.t: Right-click on a tab at the top, like Features or Sketch.
In the menu, point at Tabs and check the one that is missing.
If there are no tabs at all: right-click any empty spot at the top and check CommandManager.

entries.why: The tabs can be turned off with a right-click, so they are easy to lose by accident. Nothing is broken.

entries.title: The list on the left disappeared
entries.q: tree gone; left panel gone; featuremanager missing; list missing; side panel; list on the left is gone; left list disappeared; side panel gone
entries.fix: Press F9.

steps.t: Press F9. It shows or hides the tree.
If the left side shows settings instead of the tree, a tool is still open. Click the green check to finish it or the red X to cancel.

entries.why: The left panel shares its space. When a tool is open, its settings replace the tree until you finish.

entries.title: My view is tilted and I cannot draw straight
entries.q: tilted; sideways; rotated; crooked; cant see sketch flat; view wrong; upside down
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+8 to look straight at the sketch, or press the spacebar and pick Front.

steps.t: Inside a sketch, press Ctrl+8. The view turns to face the sketch.
Or press the spacebar and double-click Front.

entries.why: Drawing on a tilted view makes lines land at angles you did not mean. Always look straight at the sketch while you draw.

entries.title: My extrude went the wrong way, or only to one side
entries.q: wrong direction; one side; not centered; mid plane; flip; reverse; extrude backwards
entries.fix: Edit the extrude and change Blind to Mid Plane.

steps.t: Right-click Boss-Extrude1 in the tree and pick Edit Feature.
Under Direction 1, open the drop-down that says Blind and pick Mid Plane.
Type the full thickness, for example 0.500. Half goes each way.
Click the green check.

entries.why: Mid Plane grows the part equally both ways from the sketch, so the front and back of your hook match and it stays centered.

entries.title: My part has two bodies (Solid Bodies(2))
entries.q: two bodies; solid bodies 2; separate pieces; not connected; merge result; floating
entries.fix: Edit the last extrude and check Merge result, or change it so it touches the rest of the part.

steps.t: Open the Solid Bodies folder in the tree. If it says (2), you have two separate pieces.
Right-click the last extrude, pick Edit Feature, and check Merge result.
If it still makes two, the new piece does not touch the old one. Edit its sketch so they overlap.

entries.why: A hook must be one solid piece. Two bodies that only look connected will print as two parts that fall apart.

entries.title: My circle dimension shows R instead of a diameter
entries.q: radius; diameter; R instead of; circle dimension; show diameter
entries.fix: Right-click the dimension, open Display Options, and pick Display As Diameter.

steps.t: Right-click the dimension.
Point at Display Options and click Display As Diameter.
Next time, click a full circle, not an arc. A circle gets a diameter automatically.

entries.why: Arcs are measured by radius and full circles by diameter. The hook rules are written as diameters, so show them that way.

entries.title: SolidWorks froze or closed
entries.q: froze; crashed; not responding; closed; lost my work; recover
entries.fix: Wait 30 seconds. If it closed, open SolidWorks again and look for Document Recovery on the right.

steps.t: Give it 30 seconds before clicking anything. It may be thinking.
If it closed, reopen SolidWorks. A Document Recovery panel appears on the right side with your last autosave.
Open it and immediately use Save As to save it with your name.
From now on press Ctrl+S every few minutes.

entries.why: Autosave keeps copies every few minutes, but only a real save is safe.

entries.title: When I typed a dimension, the whole shape jumped or flipped
entries.q: shape jumped; flipped; went crazy; distorted; dimension moved everything; exploded
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z. Then drag the shape close to the right size first and dimension it again.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z to undo the jump.
Drag the lines so they are already close to the size you want.
Dimension the big sizes first, then the small ones.

entries.why: When you type a number, SolidWorks moves whatever lines are free to move. If the sketch was far from that size, a lot has to move and it can flip.

entries.title: The box to type my dimension did not pop up
entries.q: no box; cant type number; dimension box; modify box; type value
entries.fix: Double-click the dimension number. The box opens.

steps.t: Double-click the number.
Type the value and press Enter.

entries.why: The box opens automatically only when a setting is on. Double-clicking always works.

entries.title: My sketch is on the wrong plane
entries.q: wrong plane; lying flat; top plane; sideways part; edit sketch plane
entries.fix: Right-click the sketch in the tree, pick Edit Sketch Plane, then click Front Plane.

steps.t: Right-click the sketch in the tree.
Pick Edit Sketch Plane.
Click Front Plane in the tree, then the green check.

entries.why: Build the hook outline on the Front Plane so Front view shows its shape and Mid Plane grows it evenly.

entries.title: It says rebuild, or there is a traffic light icon
entries.q: rebuild; traffic light; needs rebuild; not updated
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+B.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+B to rebuild.
Still marked? Press Ctrl+Q to rebuild everything.

entries.why: After a change, SolidWorks recalculates the part. Rebuild makes it catch up.

entries.title: I dragged an arrow and my part changed size
entries.q: dragged arrow; changed size by accident; blue arrow; instant3d
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z.
To change a size on purpose, double-click its number and type it.

entries.why: Those arrows let you drag a feature bigger or smaller. Dragging by accident changes the real size.

entries.title: Start a new part
entries.q: new part; new file; start; begin; create part; open solidworks
entries.fix: File, New, Part, OK. Then switch to inches and save it with your name.

steps.t: Click File, then New (or the blank page icon at the top).
Pick Part and click OK.
Check the bottom-right corner says IPS. If not, click it and pick IPS.
Save it now: Ctrl+S, name it with your last name.

entries.why: Saving first means autosave and Ctrl+S protect your work from the first minute.

entries.title: Switch to inches
entries.q: inches; units; ips; change units; set units
entries.fix: Click the units at the bottom-right corner and pick IPS.

steps.t: Click the unit label at the bottom-right corner of the window.
Pick IPS (inch, pound, second).
For three decimals: Options (gear), Document Properties, Units, Length decimals .123.

entries.why: Every hook rule is in inches, to three decimals.

entries.title: Start a sketch
entries.q: start sketch; new sketch; draw; begin drawing; front plane; sketch plane
entries.fix: Click Front Plane in the tree, then click the Sketch icon that pops up.

steps.t: In the tree on the left, click Front Plane.
Click the Sketch icon in the small bar that pops up. Or use the Sketch tab, then Sketch.
The view turns to face the plane. If it does not, press Ctrl+8.
The origin (two small red arrows) is the center of your part. Start your first circle there.

entries.why: A sketch is a flat drawing on a plane. The Front Plane is the one you look straight at, so the hook outline goes there.

entries.title: Draw lines, circles and arcs
entries.q: draw line; circle; arc; rectangle; draw shape; sketch tools; curve
entries.fix: Sketch tab: Line, Circle, or an Arc. Click to start, click to end, Esc to stop.

steps.t: Circle: on the Sketch tab click Circle, click the center, move out, click again.
Line: click Line, click a start point, click each corner. Double-click or press Esc to stop.
Curve that flows from a line: while drawing a line, press A. The next click makes an arc. Press A again for a line.
Start and end points should snap onto each other. An orange square means they joined.

entries.why: Do not worry about exact sizes while drawing. Draw the shape roughly, then set exact sizes with Smart Dimension.

entries.title: Set an exact size (Smart Dimension)
entries.q: dimension; size; exact size; smart dimension; measure in sketch; set length; diameter; center to center; set size; exact size; type number; make exact; how big; demension; dimention; dimenshun; dimesion
entries.fix: Sketch tab, Smart Dimension, click the thing, click to place, type the number, Enter.

steps.t: Click Smart Dimension on the Sketch tab (the icon with a ruler and a diameter sign).
Line length: click the line. Circle diameter: click the circle. Center to center: click one circle, then the other.
Move the mouse to where the number should sit and click.
Type the value in inches and press Enter.
Press Esc when you are done dimensioning.

entries.why: The sketch is only rough until you dimension it. Dimensions are how you control the real size, and how you change it later.

entries.title: Change a size after I extruded
entries.q: change size; change dimension; edit dimension; resize; make bigger; make smaller; modify
entries.fix: Double-click the part to show its numbers, double-click the number, type the new value, press Enter.

steps.t: Double-click the feature in the tree, or on the part. Its dimensions appear.
Double-click the number you want to change.
Type the new value and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+B to rebuild.

entries.why: This is the whole point of CAD: one number changes and the part updates.

entries.title: Leave the sketch
entries.q: exit sketch; leave sketch; finish sketch; done sketching; close sketch; finish drawing; done drawing; leave drawing; get out of sketch
entries.fix: Click the Exit Sketch icon in the top-right corner of the part area.

steps.t: Look at the top-right corner of the part area.
Click the icon with the sketch and the check mark to keep your sketch. Do NOT click the red X: it throws away your changes.

entries.why: You can go back in at any time with Edit Sketch.

entries.title: Make it 3D (Extruded Boss/Base)
entries.q: extrude; make 3d; thickness; boss; turn sketch into part; extruded boss base; make it thick; make it solid; turn into 3d; pop out; give it thickness; extrued; extrood; extude; extrute; exturde
entries.fix: Features tab, Extruded Boss/Base, Mid Plane, type the thickness, green check.

steps.t: Click the Features tab.
Click Extruded Boss/Base.
If it asks for a sketch, click your sketch.
Under Direction 1 pick Mid Plane and type the thickness (0.750 is the most allowed).
Click the green check.

entries.why: An extrude pushes a closed outline straight out to make a solid. Mid Plane keeps it centered.

entries.title: Sketch on a face of my part
entries.q: sketch on face; draw on part; face sketch; add to face
entries.fix: Click a flat face of the part, then click the Sketch icon that pops up.

steps.t: Click a flat face. It turns blue.
Click Sketch in the bar that pops up.
Press Ctrl+8 to look straight at it.
Draw a closed outline, then use Extruded Boss/Base to add or Extruded Cut to remove.

entries.why: Any flat face can be a sketch plane. That is how you add a raised rim, a pocket or a boss.

entries.title: Cut a hole or a pocket (Extruded Cut)
entries.q: cut; hole; pocket; remove material; extruded cut; subtract; make hole; put hole; poke hole; hollow
entries.fix: Sketch the shape on a face, then Features tab, Extruded Cut, set the depth, green check.

steps.t: Sketch a closed shape on a face.
Features tab, Extruded Cut.
Pick Through All for a hole all the way through, or Blind and type a depth for a pocket.
Nothing cut? Click the arrow next to the depth to flip the direction.
Click the green check.

entries.why: A cut is an extrude that removes material instead of adding it.

entries.title: Round an edge (Fillet)
entries.q: fillet; round edge; round corner; smooth edge; radius edge; make it round; round the edges; make edges round; filet; fillit; filit; fillett; round edges
entries.fix: Features tab, Fillet, type a radius, click the edges, green check.

steps.t: Features tab, Fillet.
Type a radius, like 0.060.
Click each edge to round. They list on the left.
Green check. If it fails, make the radius smaller.

entries.why: Sharp inside corners are where cracks start. Rounding them makes the hook stronger.

entries.title: Bevel an edge (Chamfer)
entries.q: chamfer; bevel; angled edge; 45 degree edge
entries.fix: Features tab, click the small arrow under Fillet, Chamfer, type a distance, click edges, green check.

steps.t: Features tab. Click the small arrow under Fillet and pick Chamfer.
Type a distance and click the edges.
Green check.

entries.why: A 45 degree chamfer on an edge that faces down on the printer prints without support.

entries.title: Make both sides match (Mirror)
entries.q: mirror; symmetric; both sides; copy to other side; match
entries.fix: Features tab, Mirror, pick Front Plane as the mirror, pick the feature to copy, green check.

steps.t: Features tab, Mirror.
Mirror Face/Plane: click Front Plane in the tree (click the small arrow at the top of the left panel to show it).
Features to Mirror: click the cut or boss you made on one side.
Green check. In a sketch, use Mirror Entities with a centerline instead.

entries.why: A hook pulled in the middle should be the same on both faces, or it twists.

entries.title: Copy an outline, or turn a line into a band (Offset Entities)
entries.q: offset; wall; rim; copy outline; inside outline; border; band; thicken line; make line thick; even width; both sides
entries.fix: Sketch tab, Offset Entities, type a distance, click the line or edges. For a band: check Bi-directional and Cap ends.

steps.t: Be in a sketch. Sketch tab, Offset Entities.
Type the distance, then click the line or edge. Select chain picks every connected piece.
To make a band from a path: check Bi-directional (both sides) and Cap ends, then pick Arcs.
Went the wrong way? Check Reverse. Then the green check.

entries.why: A band from one path keeps the same width all the way around, which is what a hook or a rim needs.

entries.title: Erase part of a line (Trim)
entries.q: trim; erase part of line; cut line; remove extra; power trim; cut line; erase part of circle; remove inside arc; extra line inside; trimm; triming; trimming
entries.fix: Sketch tab, Trim Entities, Power trim, drag across the pieces you do not want.

steps.t: Sketch tab, Trim Entities.
Pick Power trim.
Hold the left mouse button and drag across the pieces. They disappear.
Esc when done.

entries.why: Overlapping circles and lines leave extra pieces inside your outline. Trim removes them so the outline is one loop.

entries.title: Draw a centerline
entries.q: centerline; center line; construction; dashed line; symmetry line
entries.fix: Sketch tab, click the small arrow next to Line, Centerline.

steps.t: Click the arrow next to Line and pick Centerline.
Draw it like a normal line.

entries.why: A centerline is a guide. It never becomes plastic, and Mirror Entities uses it as the mirror.

entries.title: Make two things touch, line up, or be tangent
entries.q: tangent; smooth; coincident; line up; horizontal; vertical; equal; relation; make smooth; line touching circle; tangent; attach line to circle
entries.fix: Hold Ctrl and click both items, then pick the relation on the left.

steps.t: Hold Ctrl and click the two items.
On the left, under Add Relations, pick one: Tangent (smooth join), Coincident (touching), Horizontal, Equal.
Press Esc.

entries.why: Relations lock how shapes connect. Tangent makes an arc flow into a line with no corner, which is stronger.

entries.title: Measure my part
entries.q: measure; how big; check size; distance; diameter; thickness; center distance; mesure; how long is it; check size
entries.fix: Evaluate tab, Measure, click what you want to measure.

steps.t: Click the Evaluate tab, then Measure.
Two circle edges: shows the center to center distance.
One circle edge: shows its diameter.
Two faces: shows the distance between them, like the thickness.
Click in empty space to clear, and close the box when done.

entries.why: Measure checks the real part, which is what the inspection will check.

entries.title: Turn, zoom and move the view
entries.q: rotate; turn; spin; zoom; pan; move view; look around; view; scroll wheel; middle mouse; middle mouse button; middle button; wheel click; spin it around; zoom in; zoom out; turn around; look at back; rotate part; see other side; move around
entries.fix: Hold the middle mouse button to turn. Scroll to zoom. Ctrl + middle button to slide.

steps.t: Turn: hold the middle mouse button (the scroll wheel) and drag.
Zoom: roll the scroll wheel.
Slide: hold Ctrl and the middle mouse button and drag.
Fit everything: F. Pick a view: spacebar.

entries.why: Moving the view never changes the part.

entries.title: Undo a mistake
entries.q: undo; go back; oops; mistake; ctrl z; redo; go back a step; control z; take back
entries.fix: Ctrl+Z. Ctrl+Y puts it back.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z. Each press undoes one step.
Went too far? Ctrl+Y redoes.

entries.why: Undo is always safer than deleting.

entries.title: Change an extrude, cut or fillet
entries.q: edit feature; change extrude; change depth; change thickness; thicker; thinner; change fillet; edit cut; pencil; edit button
entries.fix: Right-click the feature in the tree and pick Edit Feature.

steps.t: Right-click the feature in the tree.
Pick Edit Feature (the icon with a pencil and a box).
Change the settings and click the green check.

entries.why: Every feature keeps its settings. You can change them any time.

entries.title: Find what is wrong with my sketch
entries.q: check sketch; what is wrong; find gap; find error; sketch problem
entries.fix: Tools menu, Sketch Tools, Check Sketch for Feature, then Check.

steps.t: While in the sketch, open the Tools menu.
Sketch Tools, then Check Sketch for Feature.
Click Check. It lists and highlights the problems.

entries.why: It finds gaps, crossing lines and doubled lines faster than your eyes can.

entries.title: Save my part with the right name
entries.q: save; save as; name file; filename; lastname; where to save; ctrl s; what do i name it
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+S. The first time, a box asks for a name: type the start the assignment gives you, then YOUR OWN last name.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+S. The first time, a Save As box opens and asks for a name.
Type the start the assignment gives you, then your own last name. If you are Maria Lopez: SWDAY_LOPEZ.
Save as type should be Part (*.sldprt).
Click Save. Look at the very top of SolidWorks: your file name is there now.
After that, Ctrl+S saves again with no box. Press it often.

entries.why: The .SLDPRT file is what you hand in. A drawing, a STEP or a screenshot is not the part.

entries.title: Hide or show the planes
entries.q: planes; hide planes; show planes; squares in the way; plane clutter
entries.fix: View menu, Hide/Show, Planes.

steps.t: Click View, then Hide/Show, then Planes.

entries.why: Planes are guides. Hiding them clears the view and does not delete them.

entries.title: What is a sketch?
entries.q: sketch; what is a sketch; drawing; 2d; flat drawing; blueprint; skech; scetch; sketh; skatch
entries.fix: A flat 2D drawing on a plane or a face. Every 3D shape starts as a sketch.
entries.why: You draw the outline flat, set its sizes, then a feature like Extrude turns it into 3D. Change the sketch later and the 3D part changes with it.

entries.title: What are Front, Top and Right Plane?
entries.q: plane; front plane; top plane; right plane; what plane; which plane; squares; sheet
entries.fix: Three invisible flat sheets that meet at the origin. You pick one to draw on.
entries.why: Front Plane faces you, Top Plane is the floor, Right Plane is a side wall. Draw a flat part like a wrench or a hook on the Front Plane so the Front view shows its shape.

entries.title: What is a feature?
entries.q: feature; what is a feature; boss; extrude1; cut1; fillet1; steps in tree
entries.fix: One step that makes or changes 3D shape: an extrude, a cut, a fillet.
entries.why: A part is a list of features, built in order. The tree on the left is that list. Each one can be edited later.

entries.title: What is the tree on the left?
entries.q: tree; featuremanager; feature manager; list on the left; history; left side list
entries.fix: The FeatureManager design tree: every step of your part, in the order you made it.
entries.why: Click any item to select it, right-click for Edit Sketch or Edit Feature. The yellow and black bar at the bottom is the rollback bar.

entries.title: What is the origin?
entries.q: origin; red arrows; center point; 0 0; middle point; blue arrows
entries.fix: The 0,0 point of your part, shown as two small arrows. Start your first shape there.
entries.why: Snapping your first circle or line to the origin locks the part in place, so dimensions have something fixed to measure from.

entries.title: What are .SLDPRT, .SLDASM and .SLDDRW?
entries.q: file type; sldprt; sldasm; slddrw; part file; assembly; drawing; which file; extension
entries.fix: SLDPRT is a part (one solid). SLDASM is an assembly (parts put together). SLDDRW is a drawing (a printed sheet).
entries.why: Your hook, your wrench and your dogtag are parts, so you hand in the .SLDPRT file.

entries.title: What is a dimension?
entries.q: dimension; numbers; what is dimension; size numbers; blue numbers
entries.fix: A number that sets a size in your sketch, like a length or a diameter.
entries.why: Dimensions are rules the sketch must obey. Change the number and the shape follows. Black lines mean every size is set.

entries.title: What is a relation?
entries.q: relation; tangent; coincident; horizontal; vertical; green icons; little icons on lines
entries.fix: A rule about how shapes connect: touching, tangent, lined up, equal.
entries.why: The small icons next to your lines show relations. Tangent means smooth with no corner. Coincident means a point sits on something.

entries.title: What does Mid Plane mean?
entries.q: mid plane; midplane; both directions; centered; symmetric extrude
entries.fix: The extrude grows equally both ways from the sketch, so the part is centered.
entries.why: With Mid Plane at 0.250, the part sticks out 0.125 in front of the sketch and 0.125 behind it.

entries.title: What is the panel with the green check and the red X?
entries.q: property manager; propertymanager; green check; red x; left panel; settings panel; ok button
entries.fix: The PropertyManager: the settings for the tool you are using. Green check = OK. Red X = cancel.
entries.why: It takes the place of the tree while a tool is open. Blue boxes in it are waiting for you to click something in the part.

entries.title: What are the icons in the top-right corner of the part?
entries.q: corner; confirmation corner; top right icons; exit icon; check in corner
entries.fix: The confirmation corner. In a sketch it shows Exit Sketch (keep) and a red X (throw away changes).
entries.why: Pressing the red X in a sketch deletes what you just drew. Use the other icon to keep it.

entries.title: What does rebuild mean?
entries.q: rebuild; regenerate; update part; recalculate
entries.fix: SolidWorks recomputing every feature after a change. Ctrl+B does it.
entries.why: Most changes rebuild on their own. When they do not, the part looks old until you rebuild.

entries.title: Open my part again
entries.q: open file; open part; find my part; reopen; where is my file; continue working; recent
entries.fix: File, Open Recent, or File, Open and find it in the folder you saved to.

steps.t: Click File, then Open Recent. Your part is usually at the top.
Or File, Open. Go to the folder you saved in and double-click the .SLDPRT.

entries.why: SolidWorks remembers the last files you opened.

entries.title: Find where I saved my file
entries.q: where did i save; lost file; find file; cant find file; which folder; location; where is my file; where did my file go; cant find my file
entries.fix: File, Open Recent shows it. Hover over it to see the folder.

steps.t: In SolidWorks: File, Open Recent, and hover over your file name to see where it is.
Or open File Explorer and search for your last name in the search box at the top right.

entries.why: Saving always goes to the last folder used, which may not be the one you expect.

entries.title: Close without saving
entries.q: close without saving; dont save; discard; throw away; close file
entries.fix: File, Close, then Don't Save.

steps.t: Click File, then Close.
Choose Don't Save only if you really want to lose the changes.

entries.why: Once you choose Don't Save, those changes are gone for good.

entries.title: Select more than one thing
entries.q: select multiple; select two; select many; ctrl click; pick several
entries.fix: Hold Ctrl and click each one.

steps.t: Hold Ctrl.
Click each line, edge or face.
Click empty space to clear the selection.

entries.why: Relations, fillets and many tools need more than one thing picked.

entries.title: Delete something
entries.q: delete; remove; erase; get rid of; delete line; delete feature
entries.fix: Click it, then press the Delete key.

steps.t: Click the line, dimension or feature.
Press Delete.
Deleting a feature asks what to do with its sketch. Read the box, then click Yes.
Wrong thing? Ctrl+Z.

entries.why: Delete removes that one item. It never deletes the whole part unless you delete the file.

entries.title: Draw a rectangle
entries.q: rectangle; square; box; center rectangle; corner rectangle
entries.fix: Sketch tab, Rectangle. Click one corner, then the opposite corner.

steps.t: Sketch tab, click Rectangle (use the small arrow for Center Rectangle).
Click the first corner, move, click the opposite corner.
Dimension the width and height with Smart Dimension.

entries.why: A center rectangle stays centered on the point you click first, handy at the origin.

entries.title: Draw a hexagon (Polygon)
entries.q: hexagon; hex; polygon; six sides; nut shape; octagon
entries.fix: Sketch tab, Polygon. Set the number of sides, click the center, click again.

steps.t: Sketch tab, click the arrow next to Rectangle or find Polygon.
On the left, set the number of sides (6 for a hex).
Pick Inscribed circle, click the center, move out, click.
Dimension the construction circle to set its size.

entries.why: A hex is sized by the circle drawn inside it: the distance across the flats.

entries.title: Draw a slot
entries.q: slot; oval; rounded rectangle; pill shape; obround
entries.fix: Sketch tab, Straight Slot. Click the start, the end, then the width.

steps.t: Sketch tab, click Straight Slot.
Click where it starts, where it ends, then move out and click for the width.
Dimension its length and width.

entries.why: A slot is a closed outline in one tool, so it extrudes or cuts right away.

entries.title: Draw an arc or a curve
entries.q: arc; curve; round line; bend; three point arc; tangent arc; semicircle
entries.fix: Easiest: while drawing a line, press A. The next click is an arc that flows out of the line. Press A again for a line.

steps.t: Line tool. Draw a line.
Press A. Move the mouse: an arc grows smoothly out of the line. Click.
Press A again to go back to a line.
Other arcs: the arrow next to the arc tool has 3 Point Arc (start, end, bend) and Centerpoint Arc.

entries.why: Smooth curves spread load instead of creating a sharp corner.

entries.title: Make a line that is only a guide
entries.q: construction line; guide line; dashed; for construction; helper line
entries.fix: Click the line, then check For construction on the left.

steps.t: Click the line.
On the left, check For construction. It turns dashed.

entries.why: Construction lines help you place things but never become part of the solid.

entries.title: Round a corner in my sketch
entries.q: sketch fillet; round corner in sketch; rounded corner 2d
entries.fix: Sketch tab, Sketch Fillet, type a radius, click the corner point.

steps.t: Sketch tab, Sketch Fillet.
Type the radius.
Click the corner, then the green check.

entries.why: Rounding in the sketch or with the Fillet feature both work. The feature version is easier to change later.

entries.title: See the part from the front, top or at an angle
entries.q: front view; top view; isometric; angle view; standard views; view orientation; spin view
entries.fix: Press the spacebar with the mouse over the part, then double-click a view: Front, Top, or Isometric for the angled view.

steps.t: Put the mouse over the part and press the spacebar. A box of views opens.
Double-click Front, Top, or Isometric.
To turn it freely instead, hold the middle mouse button (the scroll wheel) and drag.

entries.why: Isometric shows all three directions at once, the best view for a screenshot.

entries.title: See through my part or show only edges
entries.q: wireframe; see through; transparent; shaded; hidden lines; display style
entries.fix: Use Display Style in the small toolbar above the part.

steps.t: Find the view tools toolbar at the top center of the part area.
Click Display Style and pick Shaded With Edges, or Wireframe to see through.

entries.why: Wireframe helps you find edges hidden behind the part.

entries.title: See inside my part
entries.q: section view; cut in half view; inside; cross section
entries.fix: Section View in the small toolbar above the part.

steps.t: Click Section View in the view tools above the part.
Pick a plane and drag the arrow.
Click Section View again to turn it off. Nothing is really cut.

entries.why: A section view shows how thick the inside is without changing the part.

entries.title: Change the color of my part
entries.q: color; colour; paint; appearance; change color; make it red
entries.fix: Click the part, then Edit Appearance in the view tools above the part and pick a color.

steps.t: Click a face of the part.
Open Edit Appearance in the view tools at the top.
Pick a color, then the green check.

entries.why: Color is only for looks. It does not change the print.

entries.title: Set the material
entries.q: material; plastic; abs; pla; set material; material not specified
entries.fix: Right-click Material in the tree, pick Edit Material, choose one, Apply, Close.

steps.t: Right-click Material <not specified> in the tree.
Pick Edit Material.
Choose a plastic like ABS, click Apply, then Close.

entries.why: SolidWorks needs a material to calculate mass.

entries.title: Find how much my part weighs
entries.q: mass; weight; how heavy; grams; mass properties; weigh
entries.fix: Set a material first, then Evaluate tab, Mass Properties.

steps.t: Set the material.
Evaluate tab, Mass Properties.
Read Mass. Change the units in Options if it is not grams.

entries.why: In this class the real mass comes from the slicer and the scale, because printing is not solid plastic.

entries.title: Get the tools I need without the tabs
entries.q: shortcut bar; s key; quick tools; toolbar near mouse
entries.fix: Press S. A small toolbar appears at your mouse.

steps.t: Move the mouse over the part area and press S.
Pick a tool from it.

entries.why: It shows tools for what you are doing right now, sketch tools in a sketch.

entries.title: Find a tool when I don't know where it is
entries.q: find tool; where is; cant find button; search command; search tool
entries.fix: Type the tool name in the search box at the top right of SolidWorks and pick it from the list.

steps.t: Click the search box at the top right of the SolidWorks window.
Pick Commands, then type the tool name, like polygon.
Click it in the list. It shows you where it lives.

entries.why: SolidWorks has hundreds of tools. Searching is faster than hunting through tabs.

entries.title: Rename my file or a feature
entries.q: rename; rename file; change name; wrong name; rename feature
entries.fix: File name: File, Save As with the new name. Feature name: click it slowly twice in the tree and type.

steps.t: For the file: File, Save As, type the new name, Save.
For a feature: click it once, wait, click again, type the new name, Enter.

entries.why: Save As makes a new file with the new name; the old one stays in the folder.

entries.title: Take a screenshot
entries.q: screenshot; screen shot; snip; capture screen; picture of screen; print screen; windows shift s
entries.fix: Press Windows + Shift + S, drag a box over the SolidWorks window, then paste with Ctrl+V.

steps.t: Press the Windows key, Shift and S at the same time.
Drag a box over the whole SolidWorks window, tree included.
Click the step in this page, then press Ctrl+V.

entries.why: The screenshot goes to the clipboard, ready to paste. Nothing is saved until you paste it.

entries.title: Put my screenshot in this assignment
entries.q: paste screenshot; add picture; upload image; screenshot not showing; where paste; paste not working; ctrl v not working; screenshot wont paste; cant paste; paste does nothing
entries.fix: Click the step, then press Ctrl+V.

steps.t: Click the step in the list so it is highlighted.
Press Ctrl+V. The picture appears and saves. The next step highlights by itself.
Wrong picture? Press Replace on it.

entries.why: Each step keeps its own picture, so your teacher sees every stage.

entries.title: Hand in my .SLDPRT file
entries.q: hand in; turn in; submit file; upload part; attach file; upload sldprt; turn in my part; turn in; hand in my file; how do i submit
entries.fix: Save in SolidWorks first, then drop the .SLDPRT in the hand-in box, or click the box and find it.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+S in SolidWorks.
Click the hand-in box and find the file in the folder you saved to.
Wait until it says Handed in.

entries.why: The part file is the real work. Screenshots only show it.

entries.title: It says the file is from a newer version
entries.q: newer version; cannot open; wont open; future version; 2026; 2025; incompatible
entries.fix: The file was saved in a newer SolidWorks. It cannot open here. Ask your teacher for a copy saved on a lab computer.

steps.t: Tell your teacher which file and where it came from.
Work saved on the lab computers always opens on the lab computers.

entries.why: Older SolidWorks cannot read files from newer versions. There is no way around it inside SolidWorks.

entries.title: It says the file is read-only or in use
entries.q: read only; read-only; in use; locked; cannot save; access denied; another user
entries.fix: File, Save As, and save a copy with a new name in your own folder.

steps.t: File, Save As.
Pick your folder, give it your name, Save.

entries.why: The file is protected or open somewhere else. Your own copy can be saved.

entries.title: I click a tool and nothing happens
entries.q: nothing happens; tool not working; button does nothing; clicked but nothing; waiting
entries.fix: The tool is waiting for you to pick something. Read the blue box on the left, then click that thing in the part.

steps.t: Look at the left panel. A blue box says what it wants, like a plane or an edge.
Click that in the part or the tree.
To give up on the tool, press Esc.

entries.why: Most tools do nothing until you select the thing they work on.

entries.title: The green check is gray and I cannot click OK
entries.q: cant click ok; green check gray; ok greyed out; cannot finish; check disabled; ok button grey; ok button gray; check mark grey; cant press ok
entries.fix: Something the tool needs is still missing. Fill the empty blue or pink box on the left.

steps.t: Look for an empty or pink box on the left.
Click it, then pick what it asks for in the part.
Or change a value that is 0.

entries.why: The check turns on only when the tool has everything it needs.

entries.title: My dimension is gray and I cannot change it
entries.q: gray dimension; driven; reference dimension; cant change number; make driven
entries.fix: That dimension is not controlling anything because another rule already does. Delete it, or delete the other rule.

steps.t: Look for why: the lines may already be sized by other dimensions.
Delete the gray dimension, or the one it fights with.

entries.why: When a size is already set, a second dimension of the same thing is shown gray as a note only.

entries.title: My lines will not connect
entries.q: wont connect; cant connect; not snapping; ends not joining; gap wont close; lines separate
entries.fix: Drag one end onto the other slowly and let go only when a small orange square appears.

steps.t: Zoom in close with the scroll wheel.
Drag the loose end onto the other end. Watch for the orange square.
Still not? Hold Ctrl, click both end points, and pick Merge on the left.

entries.why: Endpoints join only when one lands exactly on the other.

entries.title: My cut did not cut anything
entries.q: cut didnt work; cut nothing; nothing cut; cut wrong way; no hole
entries.fix: Edit the cut and flip its direction, or use Through All.

steps.t: Right-click the cut in the tree, Edit Feature.
Click the arrow next to Direction 1 to flip it, or pick Through All.
Green check.

entries.why: A cut goes away from the face you sketched on. If it points out into air, it removes nothing.

entries.title: My fillet will not work
entries.q: fillet wont work; fillet error; fillet failed; round edge fails; fillet too big
entries.fix: Make the radius smaller.

steps.t: Edit the fillet, or start over with Fillet.
Try half the radius.
The radius cannot be bigger than the edge it rounds or the part thickness.

entries.why: There is not enough material for that big a round.

entries.title: SolidWorks is slow or frozen for a moment
entries.q: slow; lag; laggy; loading; spinning; hourglass; takes forever
entries.fix: Wait. Do not click again while it is thinking.

steps.t: Wait until the mouse stops spinning.
Close other programs and browser tabs.
Save once it responds.

entries.why: Clicking more while it thinks lines up more work and makes it slower.

entries.title: My dimensions disappeared
entries.q: dimensions gone; numbers gone; cant see dimensions; dimensions hidden
entries.fix: Edit the sketch: dimensions show inside the sketch. Or double-click the feature.

steps.t: Click the sketch in the tree, Edit Sketch.
Or double-click the feature to show its dimensions.

entries.why: Sketch dimensions hide when you leave the sketch so the part is easy to see.

entries.title: A recovery box popped up when I opened SolidWorks
entries.q: recovery; document recovery; autorecover; recovered file; popup when opening
entries.fix: Open the recovered file and Save As right away with your name.

steps.t: Look at the panel on the right for the recovered file.
Open it, then File, Save As, your name.

entries.why: SolidWorks kept a backup from before it closed.

entries.title: SolidWorks will not open or asks for a license
entries.q: wont open; license; not starting; solidworks not opening; activation
entries.fix: Tell a TA or your teacher. Do not reinstall anything.

steps.t: Raise your hand for a TA.

entries.why: Licenses are managed by the school.

entries.title: My part is tiny or huge
entries.q: tiny; huge; too small; too big; microscopic; giant
entries.fix: Press F to zoom to fit. Then check the units at the bottom right.

steps.t: Press F.
Check the bottom-right corner says IPS.
Measure it to check the real size.

entries.why: Usually the zoom is off, not the size. If the units were wrong, the size really is wrong.

entries.title: I closed my file by mistake
entries.q: closed by accident; closed file; lost work; accidentally closed
entries.fix: File, Open Recent. If you did not save, check Document Recovery on the right.

steps.t: File, Open Recent.
If it is not there, look for Document Recovery on the right side.

entries.why: Ctrl+S often means you never lose more than a few minutes.

entries.title: The sketch tools are gray
entries.q: tools gray; sketch tools disabled; cant use line; greyed out tools
entries.fix: You are not in a sketch. Click a plane or face, then Sketch.

steps.t: Click Front Plane or a flat face.
Click Sketch.

entries.why: Drawing tools only work inside a sketch.

entries.title: Make a hole without a Cut
entries.q: hole in sketch; circle inside; hole in the middle; ring; loop; top hole; hole for the rope; nested; how do i make a hole; make a hole; hole in my sketch; top hole; hole for the rope
entries.fix: Draw a circle inside your closed outline, in the same sketch. When you extrude, it becomes a hole.

steps.t: Edit the sketch that has your outline.
Draw a circle fully inside the outline. It must not touch the outline.
Give it a size with Smart Dimension.
Extrude as usual. The inside circle comes out as a hole.

entries.why: SolidWorks treats a closed loop inside another closed loop as empty space. A circle that touches the outline breaks that, so keep a wall between them.

entries.title: Trace a photo of my paper sketch
entries.q: trace; photo of my sketch; picture of my drawing; import picture; sketch picture; put my drawing in; copy my paper sketch
entries.fix: Start a sketch, then Tools, Sketch Tools, Sketch Picture, and pick the photo. Draw over it.

steps.t: Start a sketch on the Front Plane first. The tool is gray until you do.
Tools menu, Sketch Tools, Sketch Picture. Pick your photo.
Drag the corners to make it about the right size: the top hole about 1 inch across.
Green check. Draw your lines and circles on top of it, then size them with Smart Dimension.

entries.why: The photo is only a guide. The sizes come from your dimensions, so it does not have to be scaled perfectly.

entries.title: Start my hook from my paper sketch
entries.q: start my hook; begin hook; hook from sketch; where do i start; first step hook; turn my sketch into cad; design my hook
entries.fix: Circles first: the top hole and the bottom curve. Size and space them, connect them, trim to one outline, extrude.

steps.t: Find the two circles in your paper sketch: the hole at the top and the curve at the bottom.
New part, IPS, Ctrl+S: V1_ and your own last name.
Front Plane, Sketch. Draw both circles. Size them: 1.000 or bigger. Centers 2.000 to 3.000 apart.
Draw the outside around them with circles and lines, lines and arcs (press A), or a path and Offset.
Trim to one outline. Keep the opening at least 0.500. Extrude, 0.750 or thinner.

entries.why: The rules measure the circles, so start with them. Everything else is your design.

entries.title: I keep clicking the wrong thing
entries.q: wrong thing selected; clicked the wrong line; selects the wrong face; cant click it; picks the wrong one; misclick; clicked by accident; mouse jumpy
entries.fix: Slow down: move onto it, stop, wait until it lights up, then click once. Zoom in on small things first.

steps.t: Press Esc to drop what is selected.
Zoom in with the scroll wheel so the thing is big on screen.
Move onto it slowly and stop. Wait until it lights up and the pointer shows a small symbol.
Click once. Something behind it? Right-click, Select Other, pick from the list.

entries.why: Small targets and fast moves are what cause misses. Making the target bigger by zooming helps more than anything else.

entries.title: Make a round part by spinning a shape (Revolve)
entries.q: revolve; spin; round part; turn around an axis; knob; wheel; cylinder shape; lathe
entries.fix: Sketch half the shape beside a centerline, then Features tab, Revolved Boss/Base, green check.

steps.t: Start a sketch. Draw a centerline where the middle of the round part goes.
Draw half of the shape on one side of the centerline, closed, touching nothing across it.
Features tab, Revolved Boss/Base. It spins the shape around the centerline. Green check.

entries.why: Extrude pushes a shape straight; Revolve spins it. Anything round like a knob or a wheel is a revolve.

entries.title: Make a hole for a screw (Hole Wizard)
entries.q: hole wizard; screw hole; bolt hole; tapped hole; threaded; counterbore; clearance hole
entries.fix: Features tab, Hole Wizard: pick the hole type and screw size, then the Positions tab, click the face, click where each hole goes.

steps.t: Features tab, Hole Wizard.
Type tab: pick the hole type and the screw size.
Positions tab: click the face, then click where each hole goes. Size the location with Smart Dimension.
Green check.

entries.why: Hole Wizard knows real screw sizes, so the hole fits the screw you will use.
